Create layers

Source: R/layers.R
layers.Rd

Constructors for the different types of neuroglancer layers. Each layer is its JSON state (a named list) with a class attached, so fields can be read and set with $ and [[, e.g. layer$visible <- FALSE. Setting the segments, segmentColors or segmentDefaultColor fields of a segmentation layer normalises their values: segment IDs are stored as character and colours as hex codes.

Usage

ngs_image_layer(source, name = "img", ...)

ngs_segmentation_layer(source, name = "segmentation", ...)

ngs_annotation_layer(source = "local://annotations", name = "annotations", ...)

ngs_mesh_layer(source, name = "meshes", ...)

Arguments

source

The data source: a URL string (e.g. "precomputed://gs://bucket/path"), a list with a url field and further options (e.g. subsources), or an unnamed list of either.

name

The layer name. Names are made unique when the layer is added to a scene.

...

Further fields of the layer state, e.g. segments, visible = FALSE or shader.

Value

A layer object.

Details

Constructed layers get a few default fields (e.g. selectedAlpha for segmentation layers). ngs_segmentation_layer() with a graphene source returns a graphene layer (see ngs_graphene_layer()). Layers parsed from an existing scene are kept exactly as written.

Note that, as with any list in R, setting a field to NULL removes it. Use NA to write an explicit JSON null.

Examples

img <- ngs_image_layer("precomputed://gs://neuroglancer-fafb-data/fafb_v14/fafb_v14_clahe")
seg <- ngs_segmentation_layer("precomputed://gs://fafb-ffn1-20200412/segmentation",
                              segments = c(710435991, 710435992))
seg$segments
#> [1] "710435991" "710435992"
seg$segments <- c(seg$segments, "123456")
an <- ngs_annotation_layer()
